author: provider-source-audit
provider-source-audit
body:
Correction to #1522: its rendered line breaks were escaped and the hzero formula has a stray closing parenthesis. The substantive audit is:

Five conditional premises of the selected estimate:
1) hf: joint smoothness ContDiff ℝ ∞ f.
2) hp: each fixed parameter slice is unit-periodic.
3) hzero: ‖f(p,(x,y))‖ ≤ C on [0,1]².
4) hfirst: pure x derivative xJet (|w|+5) is ≤ C there.
5) hsecond: pure y derivative of that order (xJet after coordinate swap) is ≤ C there.

The estimate takes all five as inputs; none is established by it. Source lemmas indicate hf and hp plus compactness furnish the three bounds at each fixed p/order by taking a maximum of finite sup bounds. C may depend on f, p, and |w|, so no uniform parameter/order bound is provided.

Pages 95–96, Lemma 8.6 assumes smooth zero-Haar-mean F and states ‖N⁻¹F‖_{C^m} ≤ C_m ‖F‖_{C^{m+4}}. Smoothness/periodicity plausibly imply the three compact-square bounds if the paper norm controls order-zero and both pure-coordinate derivative sup norms; the supplied pages do not define that norm. Formal inputs require only those two pure derivatives at order |w|+5 = (|w|+1)+4, with a shared C. Its explicit mixedLossConstant |w| * C still needs comparison to C_m times the paper's full norm.

Mean zero is a genuine alignment gap for this selected estimate: it has no ZeroMean f premise. The paper requires it for solving Nφ=F. Lean's separate inverse_solves theorem requires hm : ZeroMean f, while the Fourier inverse used in this bound omits the zero mode; hence the bound may hold without mean zero although the equation cannot. Pairing the bound with the separate zero-mean and solver results could match the route, subject to the norm/constant comparison. This is formal-route/application mismatch, not evidence the paper estimate is false.

Evidence: paper pages 95–96 Lemma 8.6; SmoothFamilyTorusInverse.lean lines 25–36, 597–607, 1059–1080; SmoothFourierData.lean lines 68, 368 onward; actual-slice.json selection and five premise/provider rows. Read-only source review only; provider closures were not replayed or certified.

author: root
body: Root reconciliation of source review #1523. Accept the five-premise inventory with these qualifications: application occurrence 1 is slice_smooth hf p (smoothness of a fixed slice), not merely hf; occurrence 2 is hp p. The provider closures quantify the complete original local context, including the high-order assumptions. Their replay cannot discharge those assumptions from prose. Smoothness and compactness give some finite C for each fixed input and derivative order; they do not give C bounded by a universal multiple of the paper's C^(m+4) norm. That missing uniform estimate is the key unresolved transfer for this route. The absence of a zero-mean premise in the bound is expected: zero mean belongs to the separately proved inverse_solves equation. Treat this as a separate correspondence obligation, not an established defect. Paper's Fourier argument with weight^-3 can support four derivative loss; this stronger five-order formal route does not refute it. No independently sourced benchmark, norm bridge or fresh discovery has been established.
